Types are JSON types: string | number | boolean | array | object.

envelope.$comment: Stamped on EVERY line by both runtimes, from the low-level emitter.

time.why: UTC, millisecond precision, 'Z'. A local-offset or microsecond serialization of the same instant is a different string, so any query that compares or groups on time stops spanning both surfaces.

level.why: Loguru level names on both surfaces — 'WARNING', never 'WARN'. Promtail promotes level to an indexed Loki label.

env.why: Deployment environment, resolved ENV -> NODE_ENV -> 'development' on both surfaces.

service.why: Must equal the Promtail label of the emitting process. Values differ per service by design; the key and type do not.

python_only.$comment: Loguru record provenance with no TypeScript equivalent. Declared here so it reads as a deliberate asymmetry, not drift. Do NOT add stack-parsed stand-ins on the TS side to 'fix' this.

typescript_envelope.$comment: The bots stamp these structurally on every line. Python carries the SAME key names with the SAME types as ordinary optional wide-event fields (see WideEventFields), so `| json | component="x"` still spans both surfaces — it is just not guaranteed present on a Python line. Checked as required on TS, and type-checked on Python wherever it appears.

$comment: run.py runs BOTH emitters under exactly this environment and asserts both resolve
`env` and `commit` to the same value. Types alone cannot catch this class of drift:
reading NODE_ENV on one surface and ENV on the other keeps `env` a string on both
while making it mean 'Node build mode' here and 'deployment environment' there.
NODE_ENV is deliberately set to a DIFFERENT value than ENV, so a runtime that gets

collision_prefix.why: A caller field named like an envelope key is re-emitted under this prefix rather than corrupting the line's identity. One prefix on both surfaces, so there is one thing to grep for after the mistake.

boundary.$comment: The one canonical event per unit of work.

task.why: The boundary's unit-of-work name. NOT 'operation' — that is the domain verb app code sets on both surfaces and would clobber the boundary identity. `sum by (task)` must span workers and bots.

exception.$comment: How a thrown value is described, on a real-time line AND inside an entry. Two flat scalars — never a nested object, which is the one shape `| json` cannot unwrap and which previously put a string on one surface and an object on the other under the same key.
